disease.name: Fruit Borer
disease.severity_index: Can cause up to 70% yield loss if untreated

environmental_factors.soil_conditions: More severe in rainfed and irrigated chilli crops

region_specific_information.Andhra Pradesh: More severe in coastal districts due to higher humidity

early_stage: Wilting of flower buds due to larvae feeding
mid_stage: Larvae burrow into chilli fruits, leaving black frass deposits
advanced_stage: Rotting of infected fruits leading to secondary fungal infections
Severe yield loss due to fruit drop

crop_rotation: Deep plowing after harvest to destroy overwintering larvae
soil_seed_treatment: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid @ 5 g/kg seed for early-stage protection

cultural_practices: Installation of pheromone traps (5 per acre) to monitor adult moths
Removal of infected fruits to prevent further infestation
biological_control: Neem oil @ 5 ml/L water as a repellent
Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) spray @ 1.5 g/L water to target larvae
